# Team Capability Section — Template

Document type: Section template
Use: Structural guidance for writing the team capability section of a grant application.
Replace all [PLACEHOLDER] markers with real, verified information before use.

---

## Structure

1. Team overview — why this team is right for this project
2. Key individuals with specific relevant credentials
3. Gaps acknowledged and addressed
4. Project management approach

---

## Template

### Team overview

[COMPANY NAME] brings together [BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE COMBINATION OF SKILLS — e.g. "deep technical expertise in X with commercial experience in Y"]. The core team has [TOTAL RELEVANT EXPERIENCE YEARS] of combined experience in [RELEVANT FIELD].

### Key personnel

**[NAME] — [ROLE]**
[Specific relevant qualification or credential]. [Specific relevant past achievement directly relevant to this project — not a general CV, one or two sentences]. [Any IP, publications, or industry recognition relevant to this project].

**[NAME] — [ROLE]**
[Specific relevant qualification or credential]. [Specific relevant past achievement]. [Any relevant track record].

[Repeat for each key team member. Include subcontractors and academic partners here if significant.]

### Skills gaps and how they are addressed

[ACKNOWLEDGE HONESTLY what the current team lacks for this project]. This will be addressed by [SPECIFIC PLAN: subcontractor name and what they contribute / planned hire with timeline / named advisor].

[SUBCONTRACTOR NAME, if applicable] brings [specific relevant capability] and has [specific relevant track record]. Their contribution to this project is [specific deliverable or work package].

### Project management

The project will be led by [NAME], who has [relevant project management experience]. [DESCRIBE the governance structure — how decisions are made, how progress is tracked, how risks are escalated].

---

## Writing guidance for this section

**Be specific about credentials.** "Experienced engineer" scores 1. "Named inventor on 4 granted patents in electrochemistry, previously delivered a £1.2m Horizon 2020 project on schedule" scores 4.

**Make relevance explicit.** Do not assume assessors will connect a credential to the project need. State it: "Dr X's expertise in [AREA] is directly relevant to Work Package 2, which requires [SPECIFIC SKILL]."

**Acknowledge gaps honestly.** Assessors know small companies rarely have all the skills needed. Acknowledging a gap and presenting a credible plan to fill it scores higher than pretending the gap does not exist.

**Subcontractors need justification.** Name them, explain what they contribute, and explain why you need them rather than hiring.

**Academic partners add credibility.** Name the institution, the relevant research group, and what specific capability they bring.

---

## Section checklist before submission

- [ ] All key team members named with specific relevant credentials
- [ ] Each person's relevance to the specific project explained — not just a CV
- [ ] Skills gaps honestly acknowledged
- [ ] Plan to address each gap is specific and credible
- [ ] Subcontractors or academic partners named and justified
- [ ] Project management approach described
- [ ] Word count within limit
